open_obligations.attempted: I proved the marked residual-completion switching bound for \(\mathbb E(C_{12})_m\) uniformly through \(m=2K+2\), derived the exact alternating-binomial remainder, and used the falling-factorial product identity to obtain \(n^2\mathbb E(B_{12}-Q_{12})^2\le n^{-18+o(1)}\). open_obligations.partial_result:
Work on an arbitrary subsequence satisfying
\[
n^{2/5}\le d=d_n=o(\sqrt n),\qquad \eta=\frac{d^2}{n},
\qquad h=\log(1/\eta).
\]
By \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), eventually \(0<\eta<1/2\).  Put
\[
K=\left\lceil\frac{20\log n}{h}\right\rceil,
\quad C_{ij}=(A_{G_n}^2)_{ij},
\quad S_K(c)=\sum_{r=1}^K(-1)^{r+1}\binom cr,
\]
and, for \(i\ne j\),
\[
Q_{ij}=(A_{G_n})_{ij}+\{1-(A_{G_n})_{ij}\}S_K(C_{ij}),
\qquad Q_{ii}=1.
\]
The alternating-binomial identity
\[
\sum_{r=0}^K(-1)^r\binom cr=(-1)^K\binom{c-1}{K}
\quad(c>K)
\]
and the full binomial identity when \(1\le c\le K\) give, deterministically,
\[
|(B_{G_n})_{ij}-Q_{ij}|
=\{1-(A_{G_n})_{ij}\}\binom{C_{ij}-1}{K}
  \mathbf 1\{C_{ij}>K\}.
\tag{1}
\]

Here is a completion-switching proof of the factorial-moment input, without conditioning a configuration model on simplicity.  Let \(H\) be a simple partial graph of maximum degree at most \(d\), let \(r_v=d-\deg_H(v)\), let \(R=\sum_v r_v\), and let a completion be a simple graph \(F\), edge-disjoint from \(H\), having degree sequence \((r_v)_v\).  Fix \(u\ne v\) with \(uv\notin E(H)\).  Partition the completions into \(\Omega_1\) and \(\Omega_0\) according as \(uv\in E(F)\) or not.  For \(F\in\Omega_1\), orient an edge \(xy\in E(F)\), delete \(uv,xy\), and insert \(ux,vy\).  Of the \(R\) oriented edges, at most \(4d\) have a vertex coincidence with \(u\) or \(v\), at most \(d^2\) have \(ux\in E(H\cup F)\), and at most \(d^2\) have \(vy\in E(H\cup F)\).  Every other choice is a simple, edge-disjoint completion in \(\Omega_0\).  Conversely, a completion in \(\Omega_0\) has at most \(r_ur_v\) inverse choices, obtained by choosing the residual neighbor \(x\) of \(u\) and the residual neighbor \(y\) of \(v\).  Double counting therefore yields
\[
\Pr\{uv\in E(F)\mid H\}
\le \frac{|\Omega_1|}{|\Omega_0|}
\le \frac{r_ur_v}{R-2d^2-4d}
\tag{2}
\]
whenever the denominator is positive.  If \(\Omega_0\) were empty, the positive number of forward switchings would itself be a contradiction, so (2) also covers that case.

For an integer \(1\le m\le 2K+2\), expand \((C_{12})_m\) as the sum over ordered distinct witnesses \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\in V_n\setminus\{1,2\}\).  Conditional successively on the \(2m\) edges of the copy of \(K_{2,m}\) rooted at \(1,2\), apply (2).  Since \(h\ge\log 2\), one has \(K=O(\log n)\); since \(d\ge n^{2/5}\), eventually \(2K+2<d\).  With
\[
\delta_n=
\frac{2d^2+4d+4(2K+2)}{nd}=o(1),
\]
every switching denominator is at least \(nd(1-\delta_n)\).  The residual-degree numerators multiply to \((d)_m^2\{d(d-1)\}^m\).  Label exchangeability and \((n-2)_m\le n^m\) consequently give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E(C_{12})_m
&\le
\frac{(n-2)_m(d)_m^2\{d(d-1)\}^m}
     {\{nd(1-\delta_n)\}^{2m}}\\
&\le \eta^m(1-\delta_n)^{-2m}
=\{1+o(1)\}^m\eta^m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The error is uniform over \(m\le2K+2\), and its logarithm is at most \(4m\delta_n=o(Kh)\), because \(m=O(K)\), \(\delta_n=o(1)\), and \(h\ge\log2\).  This proves the requested factorial-moment estimate directly under the uniform simple regular law.

Let \(r=K+1\).  From (1),
\[
|(B_{G_n})_{12}-Q_{12}|^2\le\binom{C_{12}}r^2.
\]
The exact product identity
\[
(c)_r^2=\sum_{j=0}^r\binom rj^2j!(c)_{2r-j}
\]
and (3) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\binom{C_{12}}r^2
&=\sum_{j=0}^r
  \frac{\mathbb E(C_{12})_{2r-j}}{j!(r-j)!^2}\\
&\le \eta^r\exp\{o(Kh)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, after extracting the uniform switching-error factor, the sum has at most \(r+1\) terms, every factorial denominator is at least one, and \(\eta^{2r-j}\le\eta^r\); moreover \(\log(r+1)=o(Kh)\).  Since \(Kh\ge20\log n\), while \(d\ge n^{2/5}\) gives \(h\le(1/5)\log n\) and hence \(Kh\le(101/5)\log n\), (4) gives
\[
n^2\mathbb E\{(B_{G_n})_{12}-Q_{12}\}^2
\le n^{-18+o(1)}=o(d^{7/2}).
\tag{5}
\]
The diagonal of \(B_{G_n}-Q\) is zero, so exchangeability, (5), and Markov's inequality yield
\[
\|(B_{G_n}-Q)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\|B_{G_n}-Q\|_{\mathrm F}=o_{\Pr}(d^{7/4}).
\tag{6}
\]

Thus the switching/truncation part of the prescribed dense argument is complete.  The remaining grouped trace estimate is not supplied by the cited Xu theorem.  In that source a graph matrix \(M_\tau\) is attached to one fixed shape and is a sum of monomials in centered edge characters.  Its Section 2.3 block-value proof first bounds the absolute edge value for each shape walk and then sums nonnegative step-label costs.  It therefore does not retain cancellation between distinct Charlier blocks.  Moreover, the source's regular-graph edge-value lemma assumes \(\log n\ll q\ll d^{1/10}\), and its Section 2.2 theorem requires \(q=\Omega(|U_\tau|\log^c n)\) for a sufficiently large constant \(c\).  The prescribed order
\[
\ell=\left\lceil10\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right\rceil
\]
satisfies \(\ell/\log n\to0\), so it does not satisfy the cited trace-order hypothesis.

There is also a separate deterministic gap between the displayed estimate and the desired right-projected norm.  If \(H=Q-\mathbb EQ\), then
\[
HP_n=P_nHP_n+(I_n-P_n)HP_n,
\qquad
\|(I_n-P_n)HP_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=n^{-1/2}\|P_nH\iota_n\|_2.
\tag{7}
\]
A trace bound for \((P_nHP_n)^{2\ell}\) controls only the first term in (7).  The second is not zero because regularity of \(G_n\) does not make the radius-two or truncated-Boolean row sums constant.  The logical implication cannot hold for symmetric matrices in general: for any nonzero \(v\perp\iota_n\), the symmetric matrix \(H=\iota_nv^{\mathsf T}+v\iota_n^{\mathsf T}\) has \(P_nHP_n=0\) but \(HP_n=\iota_nv^{\mathsf T}\ne0\).  A sufficient grouped estimate would instead bound
\[
\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}
\left[\{P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)^2P_n\}^{\ell}\right]
\]
at the corresponding scale, or would supplement the displayed sandwich moment by
\(n^{-1/2}\|P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)\iota_n\|_2=o_{\Pr}(d^{7/4})\).  Neither estimate follows from the frozen primitives or from Xu's stated single-shape theorem.

For the mandated finite check, exhaustive enumeration of all \(19{,}355\) labeled cubic graphs on eight vertices again gives
\[
p=\frac{513}{553},\quad a=\frac{475}{553},\quad
b=\frac{16771}{19355},\quad t=\frac{15493}{19355},\quad
s=\frac{2059}{2765},
\]
and hence
\[
s-4pt+p^2(4a+2b)-3p^4
=\frac{360638638}{467595722405}.
\]
This verifies the finite identity but supplies neither the missing signed grouped moment nor the row-sum estimate.

open_obligations.partial_result:
All implications after the missing dense graph certificate remain valid.  Let
\[
H_n=\{\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\}.
\]
The assumptions \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) and \(d_n\to\infty\) imply
\[
r_{\log}(n,d_n)
=\frac{d_n^2/n}{\log(d_n+1)}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
On \(H_n\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}seed\mbox{-}upper}\) bounds the exact worst-case seed-procedure risk by \(C_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\).  By (8), this certificate is eventually below one, so \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\mbox{-}compiler}\) selects the seed law there; \(\mathrm{prop{:}finite\mbox{-}compiler}\) makes the selected rule a terminating observed-data procedure.  Therefore \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\) gives
\[
R_2(G_n)\le C_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\qquad\text{on }H_n.
\tag{9}
\]
Independently, \(\mathrm{thm{:}balanced\mbox{-}all\mbox{-}procedure\mbox{-}converse}\) gives events \(L_n\) with \(\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\to1\) and
\[
R_2(G_n)\ge c_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\qquad\text{on }L_n.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus (9)--(10) prove the advertised conclusion conditionally on \(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n)\to1\).  Equations (1)--(6) establish the Boolean-polynomial truncation needed on the dense subrange, but the grouped operator and row-sum estimates identified in (7) remain unavailable.  Consequently the frozen primitives do not establish \(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n)\to1\), and the unconditional matched frontier cannot yet be asserted.

prose_updates.tldr: The full matched minimax frontier is not established in this round. The inherited all-procedure lower edge, seed upper certificate, finite compiler, and the proved sparse Boolean operator theorem remain valid. In the dense subrange, a direct switching argument on the uniform simple regular law now proves the required factorial moments and makes the Boolean-to-polynomial Frobenius remainder \(n^{-18+o(1)}\), far below the target scale. The remaining grouped operator estimate is not a consequence of Xu's published single-shape block-value theorem: its trace-order hypothesis is incompatible with the prescribed moment order, its absolute-value reduction loses cross-Charlier cancellation, and the displayed sandwiched trace moment omits a necessary row-sum fluctuation. Thus the archived logarithmic risk bracket, not the proposed equality \(R_2(G_n)\asymp d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), remains the unconditional conclusion.

project_justification.gap: Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje, Corollary 5.4, leaves the identical \(q=2\) GATE game between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\). The inherited version-one work improves the all-procedure lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) and supplies a seed-design upper certificate of order \(d_n^2/n\), but the logarithmic gap remains because the dense full right-projected Boolean operator bound is unproved.
project_justification.niche: The unchanged field-tier opportunity is to determine whether typical random-regular radius-two geometry permits the inherited outcome-blind seed procedure, or another explicit procedure, to attain the all-procedure lower scale under the exact endpoint-second-moment class.
project_justification.fill: This round proves the dense Boolean-polynomial truncation step directly by residual-completion switchings and isolates two remaining requirements: a cancellation-preserving grouped trace estimate and control of the centered row-sum component. It also certifies that Xu's stated single-shape block-value theorem does not by itself provide either requirement. A future closure of those graph estimates would combine with the already established converse, seed theorem, and compiler to yield the proposed matched frontier.

prose_updates.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax remains the sole theorem-level comparator for the exact decision problem and supplies the published \(d_n/n\)-to-\(d_n^2/n\) bracket. The inherited balanced converse, seed/Rao--Blackwell construction, and finite compiler narrow but do not close that bracket. CookGoldsteinJohnson2018 controls the ordinary adjacency spectrum on the uniform simple regular law, not Boolean radius-two collisions. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, Sections 2.2--2.3, proves trace bounds for individual graph matrices built from centered edge characters; its regular-graph walk-value lemma requires a moment order larger than \(\log n\), and its block-value reduction takes absolute values shape by shape. It therefore does not supply the present cancellation-preserving Charlier superposition estimate at order \(10\log n/\log\log n\), nor the omitted row-sum control. AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020 studies Boolean graph powering under different sparse-radius conditions. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph and UganderYin2023RGCR inform restricted constructive designs but do not solve this unrestricted minimax game. KarrerEtAl2021Scale remains the intended application: a proved frontier would be a random-regular precision benchmark, not a claim about the platform graph itself.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The dense switching/truncation calculation is complete: uniformly for \(m\le2K+2\), a residual-completion switching gives \(\mathbb E(C_{12})_m\le\{1+o(1)\}^m(d_n^2/n)^m\), and consequently \(n^2\mathbb E(B_{12}-Q_{12})^2\le n^{-18+o(1)}\). The load-bearing operator step is still absent. Xu's theorem does not cover the signed sum of growing Charlier blocks with its cancellation intact at the prescribed trace order. In addition, a bound for \(P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)P_n\) alone cannot imply a bound for \(QP_n\): one must also control \(n^{-1/2}\|P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)\iota_n\|_2\), or instead bound a trace moment of \(P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)^2P_n\). The finite \(n=8,d=3\) identity checks algebra only. Failure of this sufficient operator route does not disprove the answer-open minimax target or rule out a different attaining design.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established content consists of the inherited unrestricted converse, seed-risk theorem, finite exact compiler, sparse Boolean operator theorem, and the new dense factorial-moment and truncation estimates. No full dense Boolean operator theorem or matched minimax frontier is claimed. The unresolved result remains on one assignment, fixed finite-population schedules, arbitrary closed-neighborhood interference, separate endpoint empirical second moments, and all outcome-blind graph-adaptive assignment laws with all measurable randomized estimators. No computational-efficiency claim is made beyond termination of the inherited exhaustive compiler, and no result is asserted for degrees of order \(\sqrt n\) or larger.
